propositions: One unified, tracker-neutral bridge command surface replaces fragmented Jira-specific operator tooling across CLI, Python library, and MCP server interfaces
Canonical verbs (setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) use neutral terminology; legacy reconcile and bridge-status adapters maintain existing workflow compatibility

Argument-less reconcile defaults to dry-run (non-mutating); argument-less bridge sync defaults to live (mutating); exit codes normalize to canonical 0/1/2 with legacy 3/4/75 translations for older environments
Pause state is durably remote-persisted with reason tracking and remains readable by mixed-version fleets; destructive repair operations no longer require GitHub CLI (gh)

Bridge core and delivery logic are owned by Python (src/rebar/_store/push.py, src/rebar/_lib_ops.py); runner environments (local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, bare) share one code-derived contract without workflow-local CAS loops

All installation paths (brew, pip, MCP/uvx) execute the same packaged Python implementation; ADR 0092 documents bridge-primary vocabulary and explicit compatibility-adapter decisions with convention-compliant indexing
